summary: A 1934 two-story log-crib L-4 lookout on the Salmon-Challis National Forest, volunteer-maintained and open to public use, with staffing records dating back to 1920.

facts.design: Two-story log-crib tower with L-4 cab and interior staircase
facts.status_note: Volunteer-maintained; reported rundown and in need of maintenance as of a June 2026 visit

access.note: Drive-up, first-come first-served; road may be snowed in. No evidence found of a rental/reservation program.

visit.trail_note: Drive-up access; a June 2026 visit found the road still snowed in, requiring a short hike

events.note: W.S. Meade listed as lookout man, per Salmon Herald via Idaho Fire Lookouts' staff survey; likely refers to an earlier post on the site, predating the current 1934 structure
Mr. Dempsey, smokechaser, per The Idaho Recorder
Two-story log-crib L-4 built as the first and only lookout on the site
Mr. & Mrs. Harvey Iverson and two children, per Montana Butte Standard
Registered September 25, 2011 as US 930, nominated by Luke Channer

evidence.supports: location, elevation, built 1934, two-story log-crib L-4, administered by USFS
evidence.quote: One of the few remaining 2-story long log crib lookouts with an L-4 cab, Blue Nose Lookout on the Salmon National Forest is maintained by volunteers.

evidence.supports: NHLR registration 2011, US 930, nominated by Luke Channer

evidence.quote: Blue Nose is a favorite of so many and we see why. What an incredibly unique lookout that has the log cribbing and an interior set of stairs!

rundown condition as of June 2026 visit, road snowed in
evidence.quote: Unfortunately the lookout has seen many harsh winters and it looking rundown, in need of a little TLC.

notes_for_editor: Staffing entries for 1920-1924 predate the 1934 build date given by NHLR and firelookout.com for the current structure; no source explains whether an earlier lookout post existed on the site before 1934, or whether the staffing survey's dates are approximate. Flagged in the story as an open question rather than resolved. No rental/reservation information found; access described from the volunteer survey's site-visit notes only.
